title: Waferscale Network Switches
problem: Network switch radix has remained limited due to poor scaling of off-chip IO pitches and single die size constraints. Real radix limitations stem from internal bandwidth, external bandwidth, and power density bottlenecks rather than area alone.
motivation: Network switches determine latency, cost, power, space, and capability of modern computer systems, making higher-radix switches critical for next-generation datacenter and computing infrastructure.
method: Uses waferscale integration (WSI) to increase switch substrate beyond single-die limitations. Proposes heterogeneous switch design reducing power by 30.8%-33.5%, subswitch deradixing to increase radix 2x, Area I/O and Optical I/O to overcome SerDes bandwidth limits, and low-latency buffering with proprietary routing for performance optimization.
key_novelty: Waferscale integration enables network switches that transcend die-size constraints to achieve dramatically higher radix by managing bandwidth and power density trade-offs.
contributions: First quantification of waferscale switch benefits and identification of internal/external bandwidth and power density as limiting factors
Heterogeneous architecture reducing power consumption by 30.8%-33.5% enabling 4x radix increase
Subswitch deradixing technique achieving 2x overall radix improvement
Complete system architecture with power delivery and cooling for waferscale deployment

metrics.other: 32x higher radix potential with area constraints alone

primary_theme: Waferscale integration for high-radix network switches
